result:
Applied the upstream change: `attrs.converters.pipe()` now only returns a `Converter` instance when at least one of the passed converters is itself a `Converter`; otherwise it returns a plain callable. Updated:

- `src/attr/_make.py` — `pipe()` branches on `return_instance = any(isinstance(c, Converter) for c in converters)`.
- `src/attr/converters.pyi` / `src/attrs/__init__.pyi` — added a `_CallableConverterType` alias and overloads so plain-callable inputs are typed as returning a plain callable.
- `tests/test_annotations.py`, `tests/test_converters.py` — updated to call the returned converter directly (`c(...)`/`p.__annotations__`) instead of via `.converter`, matching the new behavior.

All previously-failing `pipe`-related tests now pass; remaining test failures in this environment are pre-existing and caused by an installed `attrs` package shadowing local sources (unrelated to this change, confirmed present before it too).
